text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: runtime-engine pods (gpu pool gpu-eu-3) experiencing CrashLoopBackOff due to SIGSEGV. Crash rate 18% -> 27% over 5m. Affected deployment: runtime-engine-gpu:v1.3.8

emma (oncall): ack — I'm on it. tagging @raj @michael for eng-runtime/sre assist.

raj (eng-runtime): joining. any customer impact visible? which nodes?

emma (oncall): Hosted API error rate up (5xx rate +12%), small set of Dedicated customers seeing timeouts. Pods failing across nodes gpu-eu-3a/b. Crash log shows segfault in fused_kernels.so.

incident-bot: metrics: https://metrics.internal/redwood/alerts/5312345678 (error spikes + pod restarts graph attached)

michael (sre): quick tails of pod logs pls — also check dmesg on node for OOM vs illegal mem access.

emma (oncall): pasted logs below:
```
[2026-03-17T03:12:45Z] runtime-engine[v1.3.8] ERROR: segfault at fused_kernels.cu:427
#0 0x7f8a2b1c in fused_kernel::launch() 
#1 0x7f8a2a9d in runtime::execute()
SIGSEGV (code=1, addr=0x7fffaabbccdd)
```

emma (oncall): dmesg on host shows: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` and `NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU fell off the bus` in some nodes. not consistent across all nodes.

raj (eng-runtime): sounds like an illegal mem access inside a fused CUDA kernel. possibly a kernel launched with bad shared mem size or a device/driver mismatch. are we using Triton/TensorRT fused path?

emma (oncall): yes, runtime configured to prefer fused-kernel path (auto-fuse=true).

michael (sre): mitigation plan: 1) disable fused kernels (env flip) 2) restart pods 3) cordon/drain flaky nodes 4) collect core & gdb traces for failed pod(s) 5) fallback image if needed.

lina (eng-ops): I can push env var change via k8s patch. command I'm going to run: 
```bash
kubectl set env deployment/runtime-engine-gpu AUTO_FUSE=0 -n production
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-engine-gpu -n production
```

emma (oncall): apply now. doing `kubectl set env` and `kubectl rollout restart`. patching in progress.

(2m later)
emma (oncall): rollout started, new pods coming up. currently 3/6 pods Ready, rest restarting less frequently. error rate dropping.

emma (oncall): for forensic collection — collecting core from one crashed pod. Commands:
```bash
# on the node where pod crashed
sudo sysctl -w kernel.core_pattern=/tmp/cores/core.%e.%p
# copy core from container runtime path after crash
sudo cp /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2/task/*/<container-id>/core* /tmp/cores/
# gdb to get backtrace
gdb --batch --ex "thread apply all bt full" /opt/runtime/bin/runtime-engine /tmp/cores/core.<pid> > /tmp/cores/backtrace.txt
```
Please upload the core/backtrace to /mnt/incident/5312345678.

michael (sre): also gather `nvidia-smi -q` and driver version on the node; note any kernel updates. mismatch between TensorRT-compiled kernels and driver can show illegal address.

emma (oncall): collected one backtrace, pushing to incident store. snippet: `fused_kernel::compute_offsets()+0x1b4` — looks like out-of-bounds on shared memory index.

raj (eng-runtime): good. next step: if disabling AUTO_FUSE stabilizes, we should roll back to the last known-good image (v1.3.7) for safety on the GPU pool and create rollback PR. Does rollback look needed or is env flip sufficient?

lina (eng-ops): env flip seems to have reduced crashrate to ~2% and error 5xx rate is back to baseline for most routes. I'll keep new pods under watch for 15m then mark stable. If we still see >5% crash rate we'll rollback image to v1.3.7 with `kubectl set image`.

jordan (cust-success): notifying affected customers: created support tickets for three high-traffic tenants (RD-101, RD-204, RD-332). Notified them of degraded service and that mitigation is in progress.

emma (oncall): cordoning nodes with repeated NVRM messages now to avoid replication during testing:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-eu-3a
kubectl drain gpu-eu-3a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force -n production
```
Planned safe-evac done.

michael (sre): note: do not reboot nodes yet — collecting GPU crash dumps first (nvidia-bug-report.sh)

raj (eng-runtime): RCA hypothesis for tracking: fused-kernel index math bug triggered by certain sequence lengths + batch sizes under CUDA 12.2 driver. Potential contributing factor: recent kernel compile flags in v1.3.8 that changed shared mem layout. I'll open bug with logs and core attached.

emma (oncall): status update to PagerDuty: mitigated (error rate returned near baseline), customers notified, data collected (core, backtraces, nvidia logs). No data exfiltration.

jordan (cust-success): customers acknowledged; some will request timeline & postmortem.

raj (eng-runtime): follow-ups (assigned):
- ENG-RT-3421: reproduce locally with CUDA emulation & instrumented mem checks (assigned to raj)
- ENG-OPS-3422: verify driver compatibility matrix & add preflight for driver/kernel on node images (assigned to lina)
- QA-3423: add a regression test for fused kernel with long sequences (assigned to michael)

emma (oncall): handing off to @raj for postmortem and follow-up work. I'm going to sleep — oncall for next 30m will monitor. :white_check_mark:

raj (eng-runtime): taking handoff. will prepare incident report and link to cores/logs. I'll also prepare a hotfix plan to disable auto-fuse by default until patch lands.

incident-bot: incident status changed -> mitigated. incident channel will remain open for postmortem notes.
